title.narrative: Response - Recovery - Resilience for Conflict-Affected Communities in Ethiopia Project

description.narrative: The project aims to (i) rebuild and improve access to basic services and climate-resilient community infrastructure, and (ii) improve access to multi-sectoral response services for Gender-Based Violence (GBV) survivors in selected conflict-affected communities in Ethiopia.The total project cost is US$331 million, implemented over a six-year period. The parent project was financed by the International Development Association (US$300 million). The First Additional Financing (AF1, US$31 million) was co-financed by the Response Recovery Resilient for Conflict Affected Communities in Ethiopia Single Donor Trust Fund (US$28 million) and the Early Learning Partnership Fund (US$3 million). The Second Additional Financing (AF2, US$24 million) is financed entirely by the Response Recovery Resilient for Conflict Affected Communities in Ethiopia Single Donor Trust Fund.The project is structured around four components:Component 1 — Rebuilding and Improving Access to Basic Services and Climate-Resilient Community Infrastructure (US$232 million) focuses on restoring and improving essential services in education, health, and WASH across conflict-affected communities.Component 2 — Improving Access to GBV Response Services (US$101 million) expands access to multi-sectoral response services for GBV survivors, covering health, psychosocial, legal, and other relevant sectors.Component 3 — Adaptive Project Management (US$22 million) supports overall project coordination, management, and monitoring. The adaptive framing reflects the dynamic and fragile operating environment in conflict-affected areas. Component 4 — Contingent Emergency Response Component (US$0) provides a pre-established framework to allow, on an as-needed basis, the reallocation or replenishment of project resources to respond to emergencies at the Woreda and regional level, governed by a dedicated CERC manual incorporated as an annex to the Project Operations Manual.

To (i) rebuild and improve access to basic services and climate-resilient community infrastructure and (ii) improve access to multi-sectoral response services for Gender-Based Violence (GBV) survivors; in selected conflict-affected communities in Ethiopia.

condition.narrative: Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section 1.A.2. The Recipient, through the FPCU and in coordination with the participating regions,shall: (i) establish no later than 90 days after the Effective Date, and thereafter maintain at all times during the implementationof the Project, coordination units at the regional levels; and (ii) designate the Kebele Development Committees to serve ascoordination units at the Kebele, Woreda and community levels, respectively. The coordination units shall be responsible for, interalia, coordinating the implementation of Project activities at the regional, Kebele, Woreda and community levels, respectively, asfurther elaborated in the Project Operations Manual.

Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section 1.B.2. The Recipient shall, not later than thirty (30) days after the Effective Date, (andthereafter by June 15 of each subsequent EFY) prepare and furnish to the Association, a work plan and budget containing allactivities proposed for implementation in the following calendar year. The Work Plan and Budget shall ensure equitable allocationof funds to all regional states participating in the Project based on identified conflict impacts, including damages to publicinfrastructure and services as well as the hosting of Internally Displaced People.

Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section 2.1.The Recipient shall furnish to the Association each Project Report not later thansixty (60) days after the end of each calendar semester, covering the calendar semester.

Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section I.A.1. The Recipient, through the FSC, shall: (i) establish no later than 90 days afterthe Effective Date, Project steering committees at the regional levels; and (ii) designate the Woreda councils in participatingWoredas to serve as the steering committees at the Woreda levels, respectively. The Recipient shall maintain at all times duringthe implementation of the Project, said steering committees to be responsible for, inter alia, providing guidance and oversight forthe Project at the regional and Woreda levels, respectively.

comment.narrative: Committees will be composed of men, women, and youth representatives of IDPs and host communities. Operational is defined as having foundational documents, members in line with representational requirements, and an operational assigned budget.

title.narrative: Eligible reported cases of GBV who receive Post Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) Treatment within 72 hours by OSCs, health providers, and community service providers supported by the project

comment.narrative: Eligible GBV cases for PEP treatment are normally cases of rape that are reported at a service provider within 72 hours after the incident. This indicator will be calculated in relation to the percentage of rape cases reported out of all GBV cases, and the percentage of rape cases that report within 72 hours of the incident out of all rape cases reported. 'PEP Treatment' is defined as receipt of PEP medication
